rfm_tuples.R: In 2024, our net income from continuing operations was $372.1 million, as compared to $519.2 million in 2023. The decrease in net income from continuing operations was primarily due to two significant one-time events in 2023, which were the receipt in June 2023 of back royalties and interest in respect of 2022 U.S. sales of the long-acting INVEGA products... and the partial release of our valuation allowance maintained against certain Irish deferred tax assets.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify that the $147M YoY decline in NI is truly explained by 2023 one-time items (back royalty + tax benefit reversal) rather than underlying business deterioration. Cross-check Q1 2025 10-Q for forward-trajectory hint.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Verified directionally but understates the cliff: the 2023 back-royalty ($195.4M one-time) is real, but management understates the GOING-FORWARD impact of INVEGA SUSTENNA U.S. royalty termination (Aug 20, 2024). Q1 2025 10-Q (filed May 1, 2025, before cutoff) confirms manufacturing+royalty revenue dropped from $116.8M Q1'24 to $62.0M Q1'25 (-47% YoY) — INVEGA SUSTENNA contributed $0 in Q1 2025 royalty (line item zero in collaborative-arrangements table). Product sales grew +4.7% YoY ($244.5M vs $233.5M); total revenue still down -12.5% to $306.5M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — 10-K narrative emphasizes the 2023 one-times as the explanation for the YoY NI decline, but the same Final Award disclosure shows INVEGA SUSTENNA royalty stream ended Aug 20, 2024. Q1 2025 results crystallize the structural -$50M/quarter royalty headwind. Cliff IS disclosed but management's framing leads with the 2023 one-times rather than the 2025+ ongoing impact. Honest enough to pass severe-flag — they DID tell investors INVEGA SUSTENNA ends Aug 20 2024 — but framing soft-pedals the run-rate hit.

rfm_tuples.R: Revenues from our collaborative arrangements with Janssen accounted for approximately 17%, 31% and 15% of our consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. ... we were entitled to royalty revenues from Janssen related to net sales of INVEGA SUSTENNA through August 20, 2024, INVEGA TRINZA through the second quarter of 2030 ... and INVEGA HAFYERA through May 2030 ...
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm the August 20, 2024 termination date and its impact. Mode B: derive what fraction of the remaining 17% Janssen revenue is INVEGA SUSTENNA (the part going to zero) vs. INVEGA TRINZA/HAFYERA (continuing through 2030). Validate via Q1 2025 product-by-product table.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q line items confirm: long-acting INVEGA products royalty Q1 2025 = $17.7M (TRINZA+HAFYERA only; SUSTENNA = $0); vs ~$50M+/Q in 2024 when SUSTENNA was alive. Implies ~60-70% of FY24 long-acting INVEGA royalty was SUSTENNA-driven and is now gone. The 17% disclosure thus overstates the FY25 run-rate exposure to Janssen (will be substantially lower) — but the underlying concentration disclosure is fully accurate.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Fully disclosed. The Aug 20, 2024 INVEGA SUSTENNA cliff is explicitly stated in three places in the 10-K (license discussion, risk factor, collaborative arrangements note). This is honest disclosure of a known revenue cliff — the framework's job is to NOT flag this as a red flag because the company has told investors clearly.

rfm_tuples.M_source: insider_vs_calendar with custom event calendar (buyback auth 2024-02-08, Athlone sale 2024-05-31, INVEGA SUSTENNA termination 2024-08-20, debt prepay 2024-12-19)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 92 Form 4s in lookback. 47 sales proximate (±21d) to events; 39 cluster around Feb 2024 buyback authorization. However, the largest proximate transactions are F-code (tax withholding on RSU vest, not discretionary), occurring on Feb 8, 2024 — annual RSU vest date that coincided with the buyback announcement. Only 1 non-10b5-1 'S' sale was discretionary-proximate. Two 10b5-1 sales by Hopkinson (CMO) on Dec 4 and Dec 9 ($442k + $1.96M) ~10-15 days before the Dec 19 debt prepayment — but these were under a pre-existing 10b5-1 plan and timing is unlikely to be informed.

Decomposed manually: no meaningful pattern of discretionary insider sales front-running adverse events. Insider behavior is consistent with routine compensation cycles, not opportunistic exits.

rfm_tuples.R: We generated $439.1 million and $401.4 million of cash from operating activities during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. In December 2024, we prepaid our previously outstanding long-term debt without penalty in the amount of $289.5 million ...

Operating cash flow $439.1M up from $401.4M YoY. Q1 2025 10-Q corroborates: cash + short-term investments ~$830M+ range with no long-term debt drawn. This is a balance-sheet-strong specialty pharma, not a distressed name.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Genuine deleveraging + capital return. Cash-flow generation accelerated even as accounting NI declined (because 2023 had non-cash tax benefit). Strongly POSITIVE signal — debt-free, FCF-positive specialty pharma with active capital return.

rfm_tuples.R: Product sales of VIVITROL during the year ended December 31, 2024 to McKesson Corporation, Cardinal Health and Cencora, Inc. (formerly known as Amerisource Bergen, "Cencora") represented approximately 34%, 21% and 16%, respectively, of total VIVITROL gross sales.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: customer concentration on wholesaler channel (typical for specialty pharma); verify these are pass-through wholesale distributors (no credit risk concentration), not end-customer concentration. Check whether the 71% wholesaler concentration is unchanged YoY.
rfm_tuples.M_value: McKesson 34% / Cardinal 21% / Cencora 16% = 71% of VIVITROL gross sales. These are the Big 3 U.S. drug wholesalers — pass-through distributors, not end customers. End demand is highly fragmented (community-treatment providers, opioid dependence clinics, Medicaid). Industry-standard wholesaler concentration; same Big 3 pattern as every U.S. specialty pharma.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a concentration risk in the forensic sense — Big 3 wholesalers are pass-through. The economic concentration is in payors (Medicaid for VIVITROL) which IS disclosed elsewhere as a risk. No deception here.

rfm_tuples.R: ALKS 2680 is a novel, investigational, oral, selective orexin 2 receptor agonist in development as a once-daily treatment for narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2 and idiopathic hypersomnia ... currently being evaluated in two phase 2 studies: Vibrance-1 in patients with narcolepsy type 1 and Vibrance-2 in patients with narcolepsy type 2. We expect to initiate Vibrance-3, a phase 2 study in patients with idiopathic hypersomnia, in the first half of 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify ALKS 2680 / Vibrance trials exist in clinicaltrials.gov. Mode B: derive — given ALKS is positioning ALKS 2680 as the pipeline cornerstone after Athlone divestiture and Mural spinoff, what's the realistic timeline to NDA, and are there competing orexin programs at risk of leapfrogging?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 80 Alkermes-sponsored trials in registry. Phase 2 / Phase 3 / Phase 1 = 17/34/25; 5 TERMINATED (small fraction). Vibrance program existence is registry-confirmed. Pipeline depth is modest — ALKS 2680 is the only material near-term pipeline asset post-Mural spinoff. Risk = single-asset pipeline concentration; competing orexin 2 agonists are at Takeda (TAK-861), Centessa (ORX750), Jazz, all of which appeared earlier in development than ALKS 2680 entering phase 2.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Existence confirmed but commercial outcome cannot be assessed from filing alone. Important structural observation (Mode B): after the Mural spinoff (Nov 2023) and Athlone sale (May 2024), ALKS has stripped down to commercial neuro products + a single orexin pipeline asset. This is a deliberate strategic simplification disclosed honestly — but it concentrates pipeline risk.

rfm_tuples.R: In May 2024, we completed the sale of the Athlone Facility to Novo and entered into subcontracting arrangements to continue certain development and manufacturing activities performed at the Athlone Facility, which may continue through the end of 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm $97.9M proceeds, $1.5M gain. Mode B: derive — what does the small ($1.5M) accounting gain on a $97.9M sale tell us about pre-sale carrying value? Is the subcontracting arrangement an ongoing related-party arrangement that creates an obligation to wind down?
rfm_tuples.M_value: $97.9M total proceeds ($91M facility + $6.9M other), $1.5M gain — implies pre-sale carrying value was ~$96.4M. Sale was to Novo Nordisk for VUMERITY manufacturing (Biogen MS drug). Subcontracting through end of 2025 means ALKS continues to receive transition payments but loses internal manufacturing infrastructure. The gain is essentially zero — this was a transfer at book value, consistent with management's narrative of strategic simplification rather than a distressed asset sale.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure. The marginal gain confirms this was a strategic asset reallocation, not a financial fire-sale. Wind-down through end-2025 is disclosed.

rfm_tuples.R: The latest to expire of our patents covering VIVITROL will expire in 2029 in the U.S. Pursuant to the terms of a confidential settlement and license agreement entered into in August 2023 with Teva, we granted Teva a non-exclusive, royalty-free, non-transferable, non-sublicensable limited license under the remaining patent covering VIVITROL to market and sell a generic version of VIVITROL in the U.S. beginning on January 15, 2027 ...
rfm_tuples.f: Verify Teva and Amneal generic-entry settlements are disclosed (Mode A) AND derive (Mode B) the embedded run-off curve: VIVITROL is the largest proprietary product; loss of exclusivity in Jan 2027 is 20 months post-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Teva generic entry: Jan 15, 2027. Amneal generic entry: 2028 (or earlier under circumstances). VIVITROL FY24 gross sales grew +10% YoY; product is mature but growing. The forensic question is whether 2025 guidance / disclosures implicitly assume status-quo VIVITROL through 2026 — given Teva license is hard-dated Jan 15 2027, there is a real cliff embedded in any 2027+ projection that management does not separately quantify.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: the Teva settlement IS disclosed but the financial impact (what % of revenue is exposed in 2027) is not separately quantified. VIVITROL is one of three commercial drugs (with ARISTADA, LYBALVI). LYBALVI is +52% YoY and patent-protected to 2041; ARISTADA to 2035-2039. The LYBALVI ramp is being positioned as the offset. Cliff timing is honestly disclosed; magnitude is not.

Consistent with disciplined cost management around the cliff, not panic cuts.

supplemental_signals.structural_revenue_cliff: INVEGA SUSTENNA U.S. royalty terminated Aug 20, 2024 (Final Award boundary). Q1 2025 mfg+royalty revenue confirmed -47% YoY ($62M vs $117M). Disclosed clearly in 10-K.
supplemental_signals.patent_runway: VIVITROL Teva generic Jan 15, 2027; Amneal 2028. ARISTADA 2035-2039. LYBALVI 2041 (newly added Jan 2025 patent). ALKS 2680 to 2041.

summary: ALKS is a profitable, debt-free specialty pharma with clean PwC audit, no going-concern language, and disciplined capital allocation ($200M of $400M buyback executed; all $289.5M of term loans prepaid Dec 2024). The 13.3% pre-cutoff drawdown reflects the known and clearly disclosed INVEGA SUSTENNA U.S. royalty termination on Aug 20, 2024 — a structural revenue cliff that management explicitly dates in three places in the 10-K. The Q1 2025 10-Q (filed pre-cutoff) confirms manufacturing+royalty revenue is -47% YoY in line with the disclosed cliff, while underlying product sales (VIVITROL +10%, ARISTADA +5%, LYBALVI +52% gross 2024 YoY) continue to grow. Forensic findings are mild Mode-B framing issues (the 2024-vs-2023 NI bridge leans on 2023 one-times rather than flagging the 2025+ run-rate impact; VIVITROL Teva cliff timing is disclosed but magnitude isn't quantified). No going-concern, no auditor friction, no covenant issues, no concentration deception, no insider front-running on inspection. Pipeline is concentrated in ALKS 2680 (orexin 2 agonist, phase 2), which is honest but elevates single-asset pipeline risk after the Mural spinoff and Athlone sale stripped the company down. Honesty-alpha framework verdict: this is a non-liar with a disclosed cliff — exactly the kind of name the framework should NOT short.
